terra.problem: The woman's account says they were alone in the house, but does not establish that nobody saw anything relevant to the case.
Nobody hiding behind the door is stated as fact rather than as part of the woman's account.
The account does not say the dead baby never left the room.
The woman says she was asleep during the alleged swap, but the text does not say nobody woke her or that she remained asleep until morning.
The room holding its breath adds a reaction the text does not give.
Sharing the baby is not the same thing as cutting him in two. The explanation equates the answer with Solomon's order.
The text does not say she spoke right away or that there was no delay.
She asks that the baby be given to the other woman; the text does not say she gave him up. It also does not state her first thought or say she acted in a heartbeat.
She asks that the other woman receive the baby, but the text does not say she actually lets him go.
The passage reports Solomon's ruling, not the completed handover of the baby.
The passage does not say where the baby goes or whether he goes to the palace. It reports Solomon's ruling, not the completed handover.
The passage gives Solomon's ruling but does not narrate the baby being handed over or describe what happens afterward.
The passage says all Israel heard of the judgment and stood in awe. It does not say they heard the whole thing or that nobody grumbled.
The passage does not say the sword was never used; it only does not describe it being used.
Saying nobody's baby gets hurt overlooks the death of the other woman's son. The passage also does not describe what happens after the ruling.
